newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian ex-health minister sentenced for graft.
newsitem.headline: Italian ex-health minister sentenced for graft.

text.p: An Italian court on Saturday sentenced former health minister Francesco de Lorenzo to eight years and four months in jail after finding him guilty of criminal association, corrpution and illegal party funding.
The court had deliberated for 55 hours before passing its verdict. The sentence also included a 3.7 billion lire ($2.2 million) fine and an order to ay 4.5 billion lire to the health ministry.
The prosecution had sought a 10-year jail term for de Lorenzo, who had faced 97 separate counts of corruption. He was not found guilty on all counts.
De Lorenzo, who was a member of the now defunct Liberal Party, was health minister from 1989 to 1993.

He became the target of much of the popular Italian outrage over extensive graft in politics after investigators accused him of accepting huge bribes from pharmaceutical companies to ensure that the price of drugs set by the ministry remained high.

De Lorenzo was first accused of illicit party funding through bribes paid by pharmaceutical companies and advertising companies involved in anti-AIDS public awareness campaigns in 1993 and further charges for alleged graft followed.
He is involved in a number of other trials.
De Lorenzo, who spent seven months in pre-trial custody in a Naples jail in 1994, won some public sympathy after it emerged he was suffering from an intestinal tumour.
Under Italian law, a defendant does not have to go to jail until the entire appeals process has been exhausted.

The former minister's sentence came one day after Italy's Court of Cassation criticised magistrates for arresting Lorenzo Necci, the former head of the state railway company, on a host of corruption-related charges last year.
The court ruled that there was a "total lack of evidence". ($1=1,700 lire)
